question: A teacher pastes a whole term of student feedback into a single chat and keeps asking Claude to summarise themes as the conversation grows very long. What is the greatest risk to the quality of her summaries?
options: A) The chat will refuse to accept any further messages until she upgrades to a higher-priced plan tier.
B) Every answer will be produced by a weaker model once the conversation has passed the context window limit.
C) Claude will delete the earlier messages from the chat history, leaving her nothing at all to check.
D) Detail from early in the chat may be condensed away, so her theme counts can quietly omit some feedback.
correct_answers: D) Detail from early in the chat may be condensed away, so her theme counts can quietly omit some feedback.
explanations: Incorrect. Reaching a length limit does not force a plan upgrade; she can continue in a new chat or move the material into a Project.
Incorrect. The model in use does not change because a conversation is long. Approaching the limit affects available working memory, not model quality.
Incorrect. Condensing earlier messages does not erase them. The full chat history stays readable, so she can still go back and check.
Correct. As a conversation approaches the context limit, earlier messages are condensed to make room. The summary still reads confidently, but it may no longer rest on every comment she pasted in.
